title: exponent notation thresholds and signed zero follow Go
purpose: Values below 1e-4 or at least 1e6 use exponent notation; negative zero prints as -0.

provenance.origin: authored for OCS 0.1.0 from the cited contract text
provenance.expected_basis: language owner decision, 19.10.2026 (D-032): Go strconv.FormatFloat(x, 'g', -1, 64) (oracle: go1.26.1, runtime values; digits cross-checked with Python repr) switches to %e when the decimal exponent is < -4 or >= 6 (two-digit signed exponent) and prints IEEE negative zero as -0; -0 == 0 in IEEE 754.

notes: Non-finite floats are not representable in the current finite float contract, so their text is not asserted.
